learningObjective: Reason about the trade-offs of static shape specialization versus symbolic-shape (dynamic) compilation at the graph-IR level.

canonicalClaims.claim: Specializing a symbolic-shape IR function to concrete shapes narrows its accepted input domain but exposes shape-derived constants and enables shape-specific downstream optimizations (tile sizes, kernel templates, memory planning).
conditions: Downstream passes actually consume static shape info (tiling, autoscheduler, kernel selector).
Verifier / type system enforces the specialized shape at the function boundary.
nonImplications: Does not imply that specialization is always beneficial; if input shapes vary at runtime, specialization inflates compile cache and warm-up cost.
Does not imply that symbolic-shape compilation is always slower; a symbolic-shape kernel can approach a specialized one for shape-insensitive ops.

sourceMappings.locator: Static and symbolic shape handling in Relax / TensorIR

misconceptions.claim: A specialized function is a superset of the symbolic version and can replace it in every call site.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Specialization narrows the input domain; substituting it where shapes differ is a shape/type violation.

misconceptions.claim: Static shape specialization is purely a naming/annotation change; the emitted kernel is unaffected.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Shape-dependent tile-size selection, kernel templates, and index constant folding all use static shape information; emitted code differs.

misconceptions.claim: Specialized versions gracefully accept mismatched shapes and just run slower.
misconceptions.whyWrong: A shape mismatch at the specialized function boundary produces a verifier error or runtime abort, not a slow fallback.

misconceptions.claim: Compiling with symbolic shapes never sacrifices kernel quality if the tile size is 'right' for all shapes.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Some tile-size selections are only optimal for a narrow shape range; a symbolic-shape kernel usually pays a small overhead compared to a well-tuned specialization.

implementationFacts: Static specialization enables: constant folding of shape-derived integer expressions, tile-size selection tied to specific dims, and elimination of shape checks.
Trade-off: N distinct shape configurations produce up to N specialized kernels (compile-cache growth).
performanceScenarios: Serving systems that see many input shapes often adopt bucketed specialization (e.g., specialize for power-of-two batch sizes) to bound cache growth while retaining most of the speedup.
